# altdown <picture><source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="man/figures/logo.png" /><img src="man/figures/logo-light.png" align="right" height="139" alt="altdown logo" /></picture>

altdown is an R package that provides a theme for [altdoc](https://altdoc.etiennebacher.com/)
websites built with Quarto, styled to mirror the output of pkgdown (Bootstrap 5).

## Why altdown?

pkgdown can render Quarto vignettes, but it replaces Quarto's styling with
its own (`theme: "none"`, `minimal: TRUE`). As a result, Quarto features
such as callout blocks, code annotations and tabsets don't render
correctly; callouts, for instance, become plain blockquotes.

altdown builds on altdoc, which uses Quarto's own rendering, and adds a
pkgdown-style layout on top. You get:

* full Quarto support;
* a familiar pkgdown look;
* links from your package's functions to their reference page, with hover
  tooltips showing usage and a one-line summary.

## Installation

Install from GitHub:

```r
pak::pak("https://github.com/BjarkeHautop/altdown")
```

## Usage

Browse around to see how it looks! If you like what you see, and want to use it for your own package,
run:
```r
altdown::use_altdown()
```
This writes `altdoc/altdown.yml`, with a `reference:` field that lists your
package's current functions in one section; edit it to group them however
you'd like, in the same shape as pkgdown's `reference:` field. It also
gitignores the files the build generates.

Then build the site:
```r
altdown::build_site()
```
A preview can then be viewed using `altdoc::preview_docs()`.

The navbar is built from your vignettes: the one named after the package (or
the only top-level one) becomes "Get started", and the rest, including those in
`vignettes/articles/`, go under "Articles". See `?altdown::build_site` for
everything `altdown.yml` can configure.

## Packages using altdown

* [jlbind](https://bjarkehautop.github.io/jlbind/)

Using altdown for your package? Feel free to open a pull request adding it
to this list.
